memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When anyone has a defiling skin disease, they must be brought to the priest. The priest is to examine them, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white and if there is raw flesh in the swelling, it is a chronic skin disease and the priest shall pronounce them unclean. He is not to isolate them, because they are already unclean." - Lev 13:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The phrase that stands out here is raw flesh. Not a mark on the surface, but an open wound that has not closed. And when the priest saw that, there was no waiting period. The case was obvious.

Some things in our lives are not ambiguous. We do not need fourteen days to decide whether the marriage is in trouble, whether the drinking has become a problem, whether the resentment towards a family member has hardened into something we now nurse deliberately. We know. We have known for a while.

And sometimes the wound is older still — something from childhood, or a betrayal from years back, that has simply never healed over. We have built our lives around it, working carefully so nothing touches that spot.

God does not condemn the wounded. But He does not pretend either. This chapter is unflinchingly honest about what is actually there, and that honesty is a mercy. You cannot be healed of something you refuse to name.

The One who invites us to come is the same One who was wounded Himself. He still bore the marks after the resurrection, and He showed them to Thomas (John 20:27). By His wounds we are healed (1 Pet 2:24).

Bring the raw place to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an old wound in your life that has never properly healed?
2. What have you built around it to avoid touching it?
3. What would it mean to bring that specific place to Christ this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You know the places in me that are still raw after all this time. I bring them to You, not to be judged but to be healed by the One who was wounded for me. Amen.
